blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top, strategic tax planning means making sure that tax is a considered input to every large decision — and nothing more than that. It is not about finding clever loopholes, and not about aggressive structures that win short-term savings and long-term problems. It is about bringing a clear, disciplined view of tax to the table when the company is deciding where to expand, how to structure a joint venture, when to repatriate cash, or how to price a major new product.

It is essential that senior leaders treat tax as a normal part of strategic conversations. It is critical that the tax team be present when decisions are made, not consulted after they are signed. And it is important that the advice they give be framed in the language the executive team actually uses — effect on margin, effect on cash, effect on valuation — not in purely technical tax terms.

Strategic tax planning, done this way, is quiet, competent, and almost invisible. It simply makes every large decision slightly smarter than it would otherwise have been.

items.q: According to the text, what is strategic tax planning at the top mainly about?
options: Replacing the finance function with the tax team
Making tax a considered input to every large decision
Finding clever loopholes in the tax code
Building aggressive structures for maximum savings
items.why: "tax is a considered input to every large decision — and nothing more than that."

items.q: How does the text say tax advice should be framed for executives?
options: In purely technical tax terms
As a list of compliance obligations
Only in writing, after decisions are signed
In the language of margin, cash and valuation
items.why: "framed in the language the executive team actually uses — effect on margin, effect on cash, effect on valuation."

items.q: When, according to the text, should the tax team be involved?
options: When decisions are being made
Only when a loophole is available
Once a year, during the budget review
After the decisions are signed
items.why: "the tax team be present when decisions are made, not consulted after they are signed."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: An aggressive structure that saves cash now is a mark of good tax planning.
Tax is only one input among several in a large decision.
Good tax planning is often almost invisible.
Tax should shape decisions before they are finalised.
items.why: Inferência: o texto rejeita explicitamente estruturas agressivas que trazem 'long-term problems'.

items.q: The phrase "slightly smarter than it would otherwise have been" suggests that tax planning…
options: matters more than strategy itself
improves decisions at the margin rather than transforming them
should dominate every strategic decision
is only useful for pricing decisions
items.why: Inferência: o ganho é incremental e discreto ('quiet, almost invisible'), não uma virada radical.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando como está aproximando o time de tributos de uma conversa de joint venture. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, a quick word on how I'm handling the joint venture with the Singapore group. I've asked two people from the tax team to sit in on the early calls — not to slow anything down, and certainly not to block the deal. Their brief is simple: listen, and flag anything that would change the shape of the structure before the terms are locked.

What I want to avoid is the pattern we fell into last year. The commercial team designed the whole arrangement, signed the heads of terms, and only then asked tax to look at it. By that point the repatriation route was fixed, and we were left defending a structure that cost us margin we didn't need to give away.

This time it's different. When tax speaks in that room, they must speak the way the executives do — what does this do to the margin, what does it do to cash, what does it do to the valuation of the combined entity. Nobody there wants a lecture on withholding rules.

If we get this right, it should be almost invisible. No heroics. The deal simply comes out a little smarter than it otherwise would have.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why has Sophie asked the tax team to join the early calls?
options: To block the joint venture
To listen and flag anything that would change the structure before terms are locked
To replace the Singapore group's advisers
To lead the commercial negotiation
items.why: "Their brief is simple: listen, and flag anything that would change the shape of the structure before the terms are locked."

items.q: What went wrong in the deal last year?
options: The Singapore group withdrew
Tax was consulted only after the heads of terms were signed
The commercial team ignored the margin entirely
The tax team blocked the deal
items.why: "only then asked tax to look at it. By that point the repatriation route was fixed."

items.q: How does Sophie want the tax team to speak in the room?
options: In the language of margin, cash and valuation
Only in writing after the meeting
As briefly as possible, with no detail
In technical terms about withholding rules
items.why: "what does this do to the margin, what does it do to cash, what does it do to the valuation."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "No heroics"?
options: The deal will require extraordinary effort
The contribution should be quiet and unobtrusive, not dramatic
The team should avoid the negotiation altogether
The tax team should take public credit for the deal
items.why: Inferência: 'almost invisible' e 'no heroics' apontam para uma contribuição discreta, sem protagonismo.

items.q: What can be inferred about Sophie's attitude toward the tax team's role?
options: She thinks they should only handle compliance
She sees them as an early, integrated voice that improves the deal
She wants them to renegotiate last year's terms
She sees them as a brake on commercial deals
items.why: Inferência: ela os traz cedo, deliberadamente, para deixar o negócio 'a little smarter' — integração, não obstrução.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We treated the tax view as a considered input, weighing it alongside margin and risk." A considered input is…
options: an optional footnote nobody reads
a last-minute objection
a legal obligation with no flexibility
a factor thought through and deliberately taken into account
items.why: Considered input = entrada considerada: algo ponderado e levado a sério na decisão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The scheme relied on an obscure ___ that regulators later closed."
options: loophole
valuation
margin
joint venture
items.why: Loophole = brecha: uma abertura na regra que se explora — depois fechada.

items.q: "The board voted to repatriate the cash held offshore." To repatriate means to…
options: hide the funds from the auditors
reinvest funds abroad indefinitely
bring funds back to the home country
write the funds off as a loss
items.why: To repatriate = repatriar: trazer o capital de volta ao país de origem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She was careful to ___ the advice as an effect on cash flow, not as a tax rule."
options: audit
repatriate
frame
postpone
items.why: To frame = enquadrar: apresentar a informação sob determinada ótica.

items.q: Valuation is best described as…
options: the cost of an internal audit
the number of employees in a division
the estimated worth of a company or asset
the tax rate applied to profits
items.why: Valuation = avaliação: quanto vale a empresa ou o ativo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas executivas sobre tributos e estratégia. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the joint-venture structure." To sign off on means to…
options: quietly ignore
reopen for debate
leak to the press
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new tax-governance model across the regions next quarter." To roll out means to…
options: abandon quietly
implement in stages
outsource entirely
audit retroactively
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The commercial team pushed back on bringing tax in so early." They…
options: resisted or objected to the idea
forgot about it
welcomed it immediately
delegated it to finance
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Everyone agreed to involve tax earlier, but the process never followed through." It…
options: was documented in full
was completed ahead of time
was approved by the board
was not carried to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving a point off the withholding rate won't move the needle on the valuation." This means it will…
options: not make a noticeable difference
trigger an audit
delay the deal indefinitely
double the valuation
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
